standard_prerequisites.name: A finite locally free morphism of degree d has a canonical norm of degree d, and the norm of a quasi-affine morphism admitting a norm is quasi-affine
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cited at proof lines 3926-3928, both statements being previous cards of this lane
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the first case by composing the norm construction with the quasi-affineness statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: The norm statement in the normal case, applicable after replacing the source by an irreducible component dominating the target

core_obligations: First case: combine the existence of a norm of degree d for a finite locally free morphism with the statement that the norm of a quasi-affine morphism is quasi-affine on the base (proof lines 3926-3928).
Second case: after replacing the source by an irreducible component dominating the target, viewed as a reduced closed subscheme, apply the norm statement for the normal case (proof lines 3929-3932).
proof_roadmap: Reduce each of the two situations to a cited norm statement and then to the quasi-affineness result for norms (proof lines 3926-3932).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a finite surjective morphism with quasi-affine source, the target is quasi-affine when the morphism is finite locally free or when the target is integral normal (statement lines 3915-3924). The counted proof is short: each case is reduced to one of the cited norm statements, for which a norm of the appropriate degree exists, and then to the result that the norm of a quasi-affine morphism along a morphism admitting a norm is quasi-affine (proof lines 3926-3932). It is H2: the two reductions are carried out in the counted span and the cited inputs are statements of the same chapter, two of which are cards of this lane.
